newsitem.title: CHILE: Latam stocks seen mixed, Chile and Venezuela shine.
newsitem.headline: Latam stocks seen mixed, Chile and Venezuela shine.

text.p: Investors can expecte a mixed ride in Latin American markets this week, with some bolsas moving in tandem with New York, while others break from Wall Street's grip to focus on local issues, said traders.
Fears that the Federal Reserve will keep tightening U.S. interest rates are dampening several markets including Argentina and Brazil, they said.

But the more independent-minded Chilean bourse is seen picking up steam, with investors feeling free to focus again on domestic themes now that the uncertainty over the Fed's meeting last week is over.

Although Santiago stocks opened lower Monday, the underlying mood is cheerful, as the bolsa is hoping that recent figures showing the economy is slowing could prompt the Central Bank to cut interest rates next month.
"There should be some refocussing of attention on the slowing of the Chilean economy," said David Hurd, head of research at Merrill Lynch.
"Last week people were concentrating so much on the Federal Reserve that they paid no attention to the latest figures."
The data include lower-than-expected economic growth in Janauary and forecasts of a sharp fall in inflation in March.
The 40-share .IPSA index ended last week up 1.43 percent at 114.54 points.
Caracas stocks are also seen ticking higher -- pending progress with a recently agreed package of social security reforms.
"We could see continuing slight rises, although it depends on how the reforms are going," said Intervalores broker Ricardo Marino.
Venezuela has signed an agreement to reform its crumbling social security system but the bill, plus supporting legal reforms, have still to be submitted to Congress.
The reforms are expected to pave the way for a long over-due restructuring of the country's bloated public sector.
The 19-share .IBC index ended last week broadly flat at 6,344.49 points in thin trade.
Mexican shares are seen treading water as investors analyze the impact of the Fed's decision to jack up U.S. interest rates by 0.25 percentage point last week, said dealers.

"Everything looks much better for this week. Now we are in the stage of evaluating the impact of the rates rise, especially on companies...which are exporters," said one dealer. The bolsa rose 0.87 percent in a short trading week to close Wednesday at 3,842.94 points.
Analysts said the bolsa is likely to find support in the short term at 3,750 points and resistance at 3,900 points.
In Sao Paulo, stocks are seen mixed as the bolsa is expected to track U.S. bonds and stocks in an absence of fresh local market-moving news, said dealers.
Brazilian shares lost 0.3 percent last week to close at 9,272 points.
Argentine stocks are seen resuming their downward trend, with investors looking to Wall Street and pessimistic over a the possibility of a further increase in U.S. interest rates, said traders.

"The market is likely to be linked again to the international panorama, as investors are fearful of a new rise in rates by the Federal Reserve at its next meeting," said Andres McKiguan of brokerage Velox Inversiones.

He added: "It seems that at current levels, many institutional investors will stop buying, as the market appears more dependent on the U.S. economy than on the imminent reclassification of Argentina's debt by Standard & Poors."
The blue-chip Merval .MERV index closed last week down 0.71 percent at 739.15 points.
((-- Santiago newsroom, 562-699-5595x212))
